Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Aegis CyberTech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aegis CyberTech's results for the Q3 2024. With me on today's call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Mia Chen, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Security Officer; Taylor Brooks, VP of Sales; and Lena Voss, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report another strong quarter for Aegis CyberTech. Our results reflect the growing importance of cybersecurity in today's digital landscape and our ability to deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. The market reception to Aegis Sentinel AI has been overwhelmingly positive, significantly contributing to its rapid adoption and driving over $42 million in new annualized recurring revenue in just weeks after launch.

Our strategy is built on seven key pillars: superior competitive win rates demonstrating product leadership, expanding average deal sizes for both new and existing customers, glowing customer feedback on our latest products and features, robust net dollar retention reflecting platform stickiness, accelerating number of new customers acquired, cutting-edge details on recent product and feature launches, and the proven effectiveness of our go-to-market strategy.

These pillars are not just theoretical—they're evidenced in our execution this quarter, where we've seen heightened demand for integrated platforms amid rising AI-augmented threats, ransomware surges, and regulatory pressures like NIS2 and SEC disclosures. Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Jordan. We achieved record revenue of $187 million in the Q3, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained healthy at 78%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $125 million. Net income was $42 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.65. We are raising our full-year revenue and earnings guidance based on our strong performance to date, now targeting 45-50% ARR growth for FY25 with pipeline coverage at 4.2x quota.

Before handing over for forward-looking guidance, let me provide deeper context on some of our standout metrics, starting with competitive win rates—a critical indicator in our industry of multi-vendor evaluations, proof-of-concepts, and customer confidence. We achieved a 68% competitive win rate this quarter, up 10 percentage points year-over-year from 58% and sequentially from 65% last quarter. This is our best in two years, across $1.2 billion in total contract value where 72% of deals involved competitors, up from 65% last year.

In endpoint detection and response, our solutions hit 75%, powered by standout MITRE ATT&CK results with 100% analytic detection and minimal false positives, outperforming CrowdStrike by 15 basis points in detection speed and Microsoft by 20% in prevention. Network security via Prisma SASE saw 62% wins in 45 deals over $500K ACV, thanks to 40% lower latency and SD-WAN integration. Against top rivals like CrowdStrike, Palo Alto, and SentinelOne, we blended at 70%, securing $450 million TCV from 320 deals—including flipping 28 from CrowdStrike in mid-market due to lighter agents and ransomware recovery, and 62% NGFW wins leveraging ML threat intel blocking 98.5% zero-days.

Regionally, Americas at 70% with hyperscaler boosts and a $25M bank deal on ZTASE TCO savings; EMEA steady 65% in regulated sectors with GDPR edges over Check Point; APAC 60% up 8 points via cloud-native XDR against Trend Micro. Trends show 82% wins on bundled platforms, 72% in $1M+ deals, validating our $250 million AI R&D like GenAI Threat Hunter automating SOC triage. We're targeting 70%+ blended next year amid platformization and threats like Magecart.

Shifting to average deal size trends, which highlight our platform-led approach, our average ACV for new customers reached $285,000, up 18% YoY and 7% sequentially, with 62% over $500K driven by EDR+CWP bundles averaging $420K in Fortune 1000 and mid-market growth via quick SaaS deploys. For existing customers, expansions hit $512,000 record, up 22% YoY, fueling 128% net retention via ZTNA/SASE upsells—like a financial client's jump to $3.8M with GenAI Shield against prompt risks. North America $320K new, EMEA $265K with NIS2, APAC $240K surge. RPO up 35% to $4.2 billion, eyeing $290K-$300K new ACV next quarter toward $10B ARR.

Customer feedback on new products has been exceptional, with our XDR 3.2 launch integrating GenAI analytics and QRKM for post-quantum threats earning 87 NPS, up 12 points QoQ and above Gartner's 65 average. 68% of top 500 upgraded in 90 days, lifting ARPU 28% to $186K. North America praises AWS/Azure SASE at 92%, 35% TCO edge over Prisma; EMEA 89 NPS on CASB GenAI scoring; APAC 76% on sovereign features. Adaptive ZTNA cut lateral movement 94%, QRKM builds PQC confidence. This informs 22% R&D spend on agentless XDR, keeping churn under 2% with 145% expansions.

Our net dollar retention of 118%, up 400bps YoY and 11 quarters above 110%, outpaces peers, with 22% expansions offsetting 4% churn. Enterprise 125% on XDR upsells like a Fortune 50 to $7.2M; mid-market 112%; SMB 108%. North America 120% on CMMC/SEC; EMEA 115% NIS2; APAC 110%. Driven by threat spikes, GenAI Hunter, Snowflake/ServiceNow ties yielding $250M expansions. Customer success and 98% gross retention guide to 119-121% FY24.

We added 452 new customers, up 38% YoY to total 4,850, driving $28M new ARR at $62K average ACV. Enterprise 128 up 52% on Nexus XDR; commercial 245 up 32% on ShieldEdge; public 79 up 25% FedRAMP. North America 278 (41% YoY), EMEA 112 (35%), APAC 62 (28%). GenAI Hunter closed 45 enterprise, ThreatLynx CNAPP 67 cloud wins. 122% DBNRR, sub-3% churn, eyeing 475-500 Q4.

Finally, our go-to-market effectiveness shines with 48% ARR to $428M, $32M net new Q3, 142% NRR, 68% expansions at $1.2M ACV. CAC down 28% to $18K/ARR, 32% MQL conversion via threat reports. Channels 65% bookings via AWS/Azure; direct 42% win rates. North America 72% rev 52% YoY; EMEA 67%; APAC 92%; LATAM 110%. Freemium 24% conversion, integrations shorten cycles 35%, AI sales predict 88%. $45M investments for 45-50% FY25 growth.

Thank you. Now over to Dr. Chen.

Dr. Mia Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Our technology roadmap is focused on delivering next-generation security solutions that leverage artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas of focus include advancing our competitive edges in MITRE evaluations, post-quantum QRKM, and GenAI-driven autonomous hunting to stay ahead of evolving threats like AI phishing and ransomware.

Raj Patel: We are committed to providing our customers with the highest level of security. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape and adapting our security posture to protect against emerging threats, from APTs to supply chain exploits, ensuring resilience through zero-trust and immutable backups.

Taylor Brooks: We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is focused on building strong relationships with our customers and partners, leveraging channel momentum and hyperscaler co-sells to accelerate land-and-expand.

Lena Voss: Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. We are using a variety of channels to reach our target audience, including digital marketing, public relations, and events, with content like our Cyber Threat Horizon report driving authority in GenAI risks.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for Q&A session. First question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Carter: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Sarah, could you expand on the drivers behind the 68% competitive win rate improvement and how it breaks down by product and region?

Sarah Kline: Thanks, Emily. Absolutely—the 68% win rate reflects technical superiority and execution. EDR at 75% via MITRE dominance over CrowdStrike and Microsoft; SASE 62% with latency wins against Palo Alto and Zscaler. Americas peaked at 70% with Fortune 500 POCs; EMEA 65% on compliance; APAC 60% building via channels. Bundled platforms drove 82% of wins, especially $1M+ deals at 72%. Our AI investments like Threat Hunter boosted POC conversions 18%, and we're on track for 70%+ next year.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Larson with JPMorgan.

Mike Larson: Great, thanks. Jordan, on the recent launches like Sentinel AI and ZeroTrust Edge—how has customer feedback influenced the roadmap, and what's the ARR contribution so far?

Jordan Hale: Thanks, Mike. Feedback has been pivotal, with 95% fewer false positives and 62% MTTR cuts in betas leading to 320 Sentinel subs at $42M ARR, 210 ZeroTrust at $31M, and 450 VaultGuard upsells at $18M—totaling massive platform attach to 81%. NPS around 87 highlights integrations and quantum prep. Roadmap accelerates R&D 35% YoY to agentless IoT/OT and edge security, directly from VoC demanding ransomware rollback.

Operator: Next question comes from Priya Singh with Morgan Stanley.

Priya Singh: Excellent results. Sarah, can you detail the net dollar retention components, especially expansions by segment and region?

Sarah Kline: Sure, Priya. 118% NDR breaks to 22% expansions beating 4% churn. Enterprise 125% with 70% expanding 28% via XDR/SIEM/CWP; mid-market 112%; SMB 108%. NA 120% regulatory-driven; EMEA 115% NIS2; APAC 110% sovereign. $250M YTD expansions from AI/ML, partnerships, and 85% multi-year contracts position us for 125%+ long-term.

Operator: Next question comes from David Kim with Barclays.

David Kim: Thanks. Taylor, thoughts on new customer adds and average deal sizes—how does GTM tie in?

Taylor Brooks: David, spot on—452 new logos up 38% drove $28M ARR at $285K new ACV, expansions $512K. GTM's channel/hyperscaler focus, product-led freemium, and AI demos shortened cycles, with enterprise 128 adds on Nexus, regional balance mitigating risks. NDR 122% sets flywheel for 475-500 next quarter.

Jordan Hale: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident in our ability to deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
